A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching title, authors, central methods and experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support a reliable comparison, including identification of retained and relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original vector- and neuron-steering experiments, response-diversity analyses and jailbreak evaluations, including extensive appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds human validation, robustness analyses, neuron explanations, additional model evaluations and non-value task experiments.

M1.justification: Difference-in-means extraction, orthogonalization, SVD-based neuron grouping, vector addition and neuron amplification remain unchanged. Restricted-token vectors, logistic probes and automated neuron explanations are introduced as comparisons or supplementary analyses, without replacing the proposed steering procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix K adds GAMBIT gender-directed translation into Spanish/French and IFEval atomic instruction-following tasks, substantially broadening evaluation beyond values and jailbreaking. Appendix M newly uses OpenWebText for neuron analysis. The original conversational extraction data, value benchmarks and jailbreak benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: Appendix A.6/Table 6 adds logistic-regression probe directions as a steering comparator. Appendix L/Table 30 adds random orthonormal directions and permuted value labels as geometric null comparisons. The jailbreak comparator set—GCG, PAIR, TAP, DR, Human and DSN—is retained from v1 Table 20 in v2 Table 26.

E3.justification: Appendix J revises reported jailbreak coverage from 500 queries per benchmark to 520 AdvBench and 400 text-only HarmBench queries. Human validation expands from 100 to 300 items. Added experiments introduce EAD, decoding sweeps, translation/constraint accuracy protocols, and additional model configurations, including larger models and a non-instruction-tuned Qwen model.

E4.justification: New analyses test decomposition stability and token-span selection (A.5–A.6), evaluator dependence (D.1), length/decoding effects and lexical priming (G), non-value transfer (K), geometric alignment against null controls (L), neuron concepts (M), and instruction tuning (N.3). These substantially expand tests of the central mechanisms and their boundaries.

E5.justification: The existing 1,000-permutation diversity test is retained. v2 adds 51-resample decomposition bootstrap reporting, Procrustes bootstrap confidence intervals, human inter-annotator kappa with a confidence interval, and cross-evaluator agreement statistics. It first specifies five differently seeded jailbreak runs with 95% confidence intervals; v1 did not specify a run count.

E6.justification: Substantial new results cover robustness, geometric alignment, neuron explanations, additional models and non-value tasks, including IFEval deterioration for two models. Appendix human agreement changes from 92.33% to 91.5% on the enlarged sample. The Llama jailbreak summary changes from 99% to 97.2% with uncertainty under a revised protocol; the detailed steering-weight sweep remains numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 newly states a cited theoretical guarantee connecting weak linear decodability to alignment with difference-in-means, together with a worst-case rationale for fixed-vector interventions. The extraction and orthogonalization equations are retained, and no new proof is supplied. Appendix O primarily adds conceptual interpretation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the central claims: intrinsic and prompted mechanisms overlap but have distinct components; prompted mechanisms steer more strongly, intrinsic mechanisms support greater diversity, and prompted-unique components promote instruction following. The new experiments principally support or qualify these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds an applicability boundary: prompted-unique steering modulates existing capabilities rather than universally improving constraint following. It introduces model-dependent neuron interpretations and hypotheses involving pretraining, RLHF and copying circuits. It also strengthens the assertion that diversity differences survive length, decoding and lexical-priming controls, although the supporting metrics are mixed.

D1.justification: New details include implicit-prompt construction and the neuron-explanation pipeline: 50,000 OpenWebText excerpts of 64 tokens, top-10 activating snippets and a GPT-4o-mini explainer. The original extraction-scoring template is no longer reproduced, while Appendix D adds a different single-response alignment template. The promise of a future MIT-licensed code release is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5 substantially expands positioning relative to sparse-autoencoder refusal/value steering, sparse activation steering, SAE-denoised vectors and dense instruction steering. Appendices A and O additionally connect the work to concept-editing guarantees, spectral methods, training dynamics and copying circuits. These extend the earlier positioning around intrinsic versus prompted value steering and persona vectors.

P1.justification: The main section order and much of the original prose are retained. Changes include localized rewrites and expanded explanations in Sections 2–5 and Appendices G/H, restructuring of Appendix A, and new appendix subsections. The existing licensing and AI-use disclosures move from K/L to P/Q.

P2.justification: v2 adds numerous substantive displays, including robustness tables, non-value task comparisons, Procrustes results, extensive neuron-explanation tables and the four-panel Figure 45. Table 3 becomes a per-value human-agreement breakdown, and the jailbreak summary gains benchmark rows and confidence intervals. Most original plots and benchmark tables are retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's visual geometric evidence and limited evaluator validation, v2 adds quantitative geometric controls, expanded human assessment and useful IFEval failure evidence that narrows applicability. These improve evidential grounding. However, Tables 12–13 do not consistently support the claimed intrinsic EAD advantage, and many neuron identifiers cited in Appendix M.1 do not appear in Table 31. These reporting weaknesses limit the net improvement.
